directive.quote: immutable source-baselines/*.held byte-copy NORMAL commit acceptable recovery evidence ONLY if contract states ACTIVE TARGET ALREADY ADAPTED BEFORE this NEW recovery baseline; NEVER claim retroactive original byte-copy.

targets.role: Canonical implementation; the public app-hardening.mjs compatibility facade re-exports this module.

allowed_deltas: Location comments and the named audit export added before the recovery baseline
A fresh canonical core contains the adapted behavior; the existing public module path is a thin re-export facade and adds no historical-copy claim.
banned_substitutions: Claiming this recovery proves the first Workshop commit was an exact byte copy
Counting the immutable archived baseline as evidence of active implementation retention

baseline.scope: The new canonical core active path is first committed as the exact declared original source bytes; a later commit adapts its imports and compatibility exports. The previous public module was already adapted. Earlier held snapshots are evidence only and do not establish this active baseline.

source_retirement.local_working_copy_state: The retired source may still exist on disk; this checks committed main, not a claim of filesystem deletion.

recovery.privacy_and_rights: Read the full immutable source and PR325 target. Repository-owned generic implementation, relative imports and comments; no credentials, customer content or attribution notices found. Avery authorized source migration and this repair. Source snapshot is inactive evidence; active retention is measured only against the canonical core.

active_target.method: Trim each source and active-core line; keep lines of length >=24; count source lines present in the core line set. The immutable archive and compatibility facade are excluded.
